journal_lines: §aSpruce stands, cold and close. §oSmells like winter pressed into wood and never let out.§o Straight grain throughout.
§aThe air had teeth this morning. Worked fast to stay warm. Good §lspruce§l take.
§aCones underfoot, all closed against the cold. A good sign for the stand.
§aSnow fell off a branch when I made the cut. Landed on the muzzle. Worked faster after that.
§aSap frozen in beads on the bark. §oSmelled sharp and clean when the axe broke through.§o Spruce inside, tight-grained.
§aOld axe marks in a trunk already down. Someone else's work, abandoned. Took what was left.
§aWind through §lspruce§l makes a sound nothing else makes. Listened to it longer than necessary.
§aBreath fogged on the first swing. Still fogged on the last. Cold work. Good timber.
§aA grouse went up from the snow at my feet. §oHeart loud for a moment.§o Then back to work.
§aFallen spruce half-buried in the drift. Older than last winter. Wood still good inside.
